title: Here's What Key Metrics Tell Us About Figma, Inc. (FIG) Q3 Earnings
author: Na
description: Figma Inc. reported $391.42 million in revenue for Q3 2026, up 42.8% year-over-year and beating consensus estimates by 4.14%. The company delivered $0.10 EPS, doubling the $0.05 consensus estimate. However, paid customers with >$10,000 ARR slightly missed analyst expectations at 16,566 versus 16,766 estimated. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong revenue growth of 42.8% YoY with a 4.14% beat on consensus estimates. EPS doubled expectations at $0.10 vs. $0.05 estimate. Net Dollar Retention Rate of 131% exceeded the 129% estimate, indicating healthy customer expansion. Minor miss on high-ARR customer count was offset by overall strong financial performance and Buy rating.

title: Arista Networks vs. Figma: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Brendan Coffey
description: Arista Networks and Figma represent different investment profiles in the tech sector. Arista Networks demonstrates strong profitability with 39% net margins, zero debt, and expected 40% revenue growth to $12.6B in fiscal 2026. Figma shows rapid 41% revenue growth but remains unprofitable with a $1.3B net loss and significant stock-based compensation. The article recommends Arista Networks as the better buy in 2026 due to its established profitability, lower forward P/E ratio, and growing earnings despite a higher price-to-sales valuation.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong profitability with 39% net margins, zero debt, 28.6% revenue growth to $9B in FY2025, expected 40% growth to $12.6B in fiscal 2026, and growing net income. Benefits from AI-driven cloud infrastructure spending. Lower forward P/E ratio (41.6x) despite higher price-to-sales ratio.

Demonstrates rapid 41% revenue growth to $1.1B in FY2025 with expected 39% growth to $1.47B, but remains unprofitable with $1.3B net loss. Stock-based compensation inflates reported cash flow. Expected to reduce losses but remain unprofitable. Higher forward P/E ratio (84.3x) reflects growth expectations but lacks profitability.
Mentioned as a key supplier of merchant silicon switching chips to Arista Networks. Represents a concentration risk for Arista, as supply shortages or collaboration failures could harm operations.

Figma relies entirely on Amazon Web Services (AWS) for hosting infrastructure. Represents a dependency risk, as service interruptions or price increases could disrupt Figma's business or profitability.

title: Palantir Technologies vs. Figma: Comparing Revenue Growth Trends
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: Palantir Technologies and Figma both demonstrated consistent quarter-over-quarter revenue growth over eight quarters, with Palantir's quarterly revenue nearly tripling Figma's. Palantir generated $1.9 billion in Q2 2026 revenue driven by government contracts and AI platform demand, while Figma achieved $370.1 million with a 48% year-over-year increase, bolstered by new AI credit monetization. Both companies show strong growth trajectories in their respective markets.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Palantir demonstrates accelerating revenue growth with consistent quarter-over-quarter increases, reaching $1.9 billion in Q2 2026. The company benefits from government contracts, commercial customers, and AI platform adoption, with management forecasting continued expansion to $2.2 billion in Q3.

Figma shows strong growth within its design-focused niche with 48% year-over-year revenue increase in Q2 2026. The company successfully monetized AI credits as a new revenue stream and raised full-year guidance, demonstrating effective business model expansion despite lower absolute revenue compared to Palantir.
NVIDIA is mentioned only as a collaboration partner with Palantir for supply chain management. No direct business impact or performance metrics are discussed, warranting a neutral sentiment.

title: Is Anthropic a SaaS Stock? Here's How It Stacks Up With the Other Top Software Players
author: Jeremy Bowman
description: Anthropic released its S-1 filing targeting a $2 trillion valuation ahead of its IPO. While not officially calling itself a SaaS company, Anthropic operates like one with subscription-based products and uses SaaS metrics. At a P/S ratio of 30, it appears attractively valued compared to peers, though it carries unique risks from massive cloud spending commitments. The company's rapid 50% sequential revenue growth and profitability on an adjusted basis support the valuation.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Used as a valuation comparison point with P/S ratio of 25.4, similar to Anthropic's 30x multiple, but no direct impact mentioned.
Referenced as a SaaS valuation benchmark with P/S ratio of 21.9, used for comparative analysis but no direct impact mentioned.
Mentioned as a traditional SaaS company comparison point with significantly more employees (83,000) but lower revenue than Anthropic's run rate.
Stock plunged when Anthropic introduced Claude Design, positioning Anthropic as a direct competitor in the design software space.
